messages:
Jordan: spinning up this thread for a few follow-ups after today's all-hands on capacity. main asks: holiday traffic behaviour, billing implications for failovers, and cold-start mitigation.

Priya: thanks  are we expecting different autoscaler behavior for holiday promos vs normal peak? e.g., more aggressive pre-warming?

Diego: yes  we're enabling predictive pre-warm for flagged promos. policy: if a promo is scheduled and tagged in the calendar, autoscaler will create a 24h pre-warm window based on forecasted 95th percentile load.

Maya: clarification: pre-warm uses non-preemptible capacity where possible. if the forecast is uncertain we'll allocate a smaller warm buffer and rely on burst pool.

Jordan: billing Q: when we route to fallback region due to capacity, who gets billed at what rate? customers asked if they pay for cross-region premium.

Priya: current billing rules: customers are billed based on the region that served the tokens. if the fallback region has a higher regional multiplier, they'll see that reflected. for pinned-customers with `fallback_policy: none` we return an error instead of cross-region billing.

Diego: ops note  we plan to add an opt-in `cost_protection: true` flag. if set, router will prefer cheaper fallback options or throttle rather than use an expensive region. design doc ETA: end of sprint.

Support_Bot: FYI: created internal ticket RW-2201 to track `cost_protection` feature requests from sales.

Maya: cold-starts: we're implementing a tiny steady-state daemon (nano-warmers) in each zone to keep KV shards and the model KV cache warm. this reduces tail latency on first requests after idle.

Jordan: how do nano-warmers affect unit cost? will they be charged continuously?

Maya: they're lightweight (single vCPU per zone + micro-GPU warm workers). cost is negligible relative to model infra; we'll roll them under the infra overhead bucket, not per-customer.

Priya: routing detail: is the failover sticky per-session or per-request? customers using streaming want continuity.

Diego: failover is sticky per-routing-key for the duration of a short session (default 2m). after that, routing reevaluates. you can set `session_affinity` in the route to extend stickiness.

Jordan: any changes to SLAs during predicted-degraded windows (promo pre-warm vs actual overload)?

Maya: SLAs don't change, but we will surface a "degraded mode" banner for the duration of promo windows if teams opt into cheaper fallback policies. enterprise customers with reserved capacity get priority and a separate SLA pledge.

infra-bot: [deploy] promo pre-warm scheduler v2 deployed by @Diego  change: 6772  logs: https://redwood.internal/infra/logs/6772 :rocket:

Priya: follow-up: support playbook? What should CS tell customers when they see cross-region routing and cost differences?

Support_Bot: Draft blurb: "If your requests were routed to a different region due to capacity, tokens are billed in the region that served them. To avoid cross-region routing, set `fallback_policy: none` or pin to Dedicated capacity. Contact support if you need assistance." Posting to #customer-success for review.

Jordan: nice. final ask: can oncall get a one-line alert that includes "region, reason (promowarm|overflow|preemptible) and impacted routes" so we don't open long investigations?

Diego: agreed  adding a compact alert payload to the autoscaler in next patch. prototype will include `region|reason|routes:count`.

Maya: action items I'm taking: 1) publish nano-warmer spec and cost analysis by Thursday, 2) coordinate `cost_protection` doc with billing, 3) add sticky-failover docs and `session_affinity` knobs to route docs, 4) ask SRE to add the compact alert. tagging @Diego @Priya.

Priya: I'll review the billing language and the support blurb.

Diego: I'll land the autoscaler alert prototype and follow up with a short demo in #eng-oncall.

Jordan: thanks all  please emoji-react to confirm you saw the asks. :thumbsup:

Maya: :thumbsup:

Priya: :eyes:

Diego: :raised_hands:

Support_Bot: :white_check_mark:
